question: Are AB07 extra17.579129859mm physically necessary for fixed hardware, or conditionally required by the AB06 donor-relative calibration target?
scope: Conceptual and repository-source review before reading any new variant results; no Claude or inference accessed, no native/solver/FK executed by reviewer. Existing input sources are read only.

protocol_2x2.case_definition: Modify only AB07 anatomical-model distal parent-mount Y and the ankle column in its complete original static calibration motion. Recalibrate the same12 left markers, then solve a fresh whole-trial marker IK in every case. A case is the resulting model plus its own full IK; no reused current/pre-ground IK or mixed pose/model cells.
constant_sources: Own raw healthy anatomy and current anatomical base hip/proximal fit
All static biological/knee poses, acquisition clocks and raw static/dynamic TRC
Marker identities/remap rule and calibration stride1/all-overlap averaging
Solver Python/backend/version, Inf constraints, accuracy1e-5, all28markers weight1, no coordinate file
Full dynamic acquisition, measured GRF and fixed contact/binary profiles
guards: Dedicated absent case folders; no operational promotion or old-artifact edits
Input and executable source hashes before/after; full model/static-motion mutation whitelist
Model/marker/TRC/IK actual-setup hash bindings, complete21-coordinate finite output and coverage
Registered long/+angle endpoint reproduces current full model/IK semantically/numerically; compare hashes with metadata differences explained
Short/zero endpoint is freshly prepared under the same current recipe; archived pre-registration provenance is comparison evidence only
Downstream native1ms+exactHS/TO/nextHS common grid; preserve original event timestamps; never phase-retime to improve contact

estimands.end_to_end_response: Within-AB07 effect of each calibration choice and interaction on new whole-IK poses, ankle center, fixed-profile reference contact and marker residuals. Interventions include downstream free-marker fitting and IK response, not isolated geometric displacement.
estimands.conditional_effects: Report long−short at each fixed angle, plus angle+−zero at each fixed length; interaction=(long,+−short,+)−(long,0−short,0). No single unique contribution split without an additional allocation convention.
metrics: Own healthy functional ankle-center and anatomical length departures
STL minimum clearance and foot pitch at static poses and dynamic stance, with plane specified
Per-sphere signed raw depth versus positive penetration, force and impulse; basis07 separated
Stance/swing and full frozen-cycle duration-weighted force/impulse
Signed/per-marker fit residuals and native unfiltered IK errors reported separately from filtered reference FK
estimands.interpretation: These are conditional direct-reference/calibration effects, not causal percentages of the saved dynamics, nor demonstrations that matching measured healthy GRF qualifies prosthetic hardware.

registration_identifiability.equations: alpha solves median donor STL pitch; deltaY solves median[h_subject(alpha)+slope_i*deltaY] = median donor clearance. With positive slopes, the second root is unique for that alpha and target.
registration_identifiability.inference: Uniqueness establishes the solution to the chosen donor benchmark. It does not identify a measured physical ankle position, hardware mounting requirement or floor. These2 target constraints consume the2 adjustable degrees of freedom and can override the preceding anatomical length ratio.
registration_identifiability.free_marker_problem: Static marker fitting freely estimates local coordinates. Moving the mount or rotating the calibration foot also moves its inferred marker offsets; in-sample marker agreement cannot independently identify the hardware origin or prove length necessary. Whole dynamic marker IK can reveal conditioning/generalization but remains derived from these offsets.
registration_identifiability.anatomy_requirement: If final healthy-relative shank proportion must be preserved, fixing short length is a legitimate hard constraint. The current long registered value departs from that requirement by design; whether this is an acceptable hardware adaptation needs a separately defined physical criterion.

plane_origin_invariance.assumptions: Same plane normal and common origin change applied to both subject-before and donor-target; all poses and STL fixed.
plane_origin_invariance.proof: For origin o→o+d, every height h_i→h_i−n·d and target median h_D→median h_D−n·d. Pitch atan2(n·R eX,n·R eY) and slope n·R_tibia eY do not involve origin. Thus median[h_i(alpha)+s_i deltaY]−h_D is unchanged for every deltaY, so alpha and the unique root are unchanged.
plane_origin_invariance.limitation: Changing normal, donor pose/pitch, reference geometry, or shifting only one side is a different intervention. This invariance does not certify either absolute plane as a physical floor and does not apply to moving the force plane alone.

bounded_discriminants.supports: Compare functional healthy joint centers, contralateral chain and static marker observations in one acquisition frame, with explicit uncertainties and articulated versus rigid-foot geometry.
bounded_discriminants.does_not_support: Generic healthy visual foot mesh, heel/toe marker heights or donor clearance alone cannot certify physical prosthetic shoe/sole/floor.

bounded_discriminants.supports: At short length, assess feasible foot/calibration orientation under a declared independent sole/floor/contact criterion and unchanged biological poses. Report residual donor pitch/clearance separately instead of forcing both donor targets.
bounded_discriminants.does_not_support: A different arbitrary plane or donor pitch yielding lower force is not independent evidence of a correct assembly. No tuning to measured GRF or free pelvis translation permitted.

bounded_discriminants.supports: Extra length is physically supported only if short-length assembly cannot satisfy independently justified hardware/ground/joint-center constraints within allowed orientation/uncertainty, while the long assembly can.
bounded_discriminants.does_not_support: Failure to satisfy both donor-derived pitch/clearance targets at short length proves incompatibility with that benchmark only.

bounded_discriminants.supports: The2x2 establishes whether length, static marker orientation, or their interaction drives the reference-force difference under the same raw source and profile.
bounded_discriminants.does_not_support: Force closer to healthy GRF or good marker RMS does not choose a physically correct mount; sphere contact patches are empirical and differ from STL hardware.

decision_classes.donor_target_necessity: Proven by current solver constraints, conditional on donor target and fixed source poses; physical need remains unproved.
decision_classes.verified_preservation_conflict: Final shank ratio differs from the anatomical-fit ratio. It is a protocol/design conflict if the final ratio is a required invariant.
decision_classes.physical_error: Requires an independently anchored geometric or assembly constraint violated beyond uncertainty; not solely reference-force mismatch.
decision_classes.necessary_adaptation: Requires independent evidence that fixed hardware cannot meet those valid constraints at anatomy-preserving length, plus acceptable mounting change.
decision_classes.not_identified: Retain explicit uncertainty if data constrain only virtual anatomical markers, donor benchmark and empirical contact.

next_review: Peer review variants/prepare_mount_variants.py and protocol when published; constraints FK output when available. No case runner invoked by this reviewer.
